chunks: And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān and Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning a man who cut off the head of a dead person:
He said: “The diyah is upon him, because his sanctity in death is like his sanctity while he is alive.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: the prescribed blood-money or legal compensation due for the offense
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the dead person whose bodily sanctity is being discussed
key_terms.حَيٌّ: alive, indicating the comparison with the person’s sanctity during life
key_terms.حُرْمَتَهُ: his inviolability or sanctity, which remains protected after death
key_terms.رَأْسَ: the head, the severed body part mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is there diyah for mutilating the body of a dead person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that cutting off the head of a dead person incurs diyah. It establishes that the bodily sanctity of the deceased remains protected after death just as it was during life.
